name: c.i R^2-->R^2 partial derivatives
questiontext:
Let \( f:R^2 \rightarrow R^2 \) defined as:

\(f(x,y)=({{CT:0}} , {{CT:1}})\)


Calculate the differential of \(f(x,y)\): [[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]]


Calculate the linear approximation for the function in a nearby point for each coordinate:

\(f({{CT:2}}+\frac{{{CT:3}}}{100},{{CT:4}}+\frac{{{CT:5}}}{100})\) 

[[input:ans2]] [[validation:ans2]]

prts.name: prt1

on_false.feedback:
Not all of the partial derivatives are correct.
\( \frac{\partial f_1}{\partial x}(x,y) {@feed[1]@} \) 
\( \frac{\partial f_1}{\partial y}(x,y) {@feed[2]@} \) 
\( \frac{\partial f_2}{\partial x}(x,y) {@feed[3]@} \) 
\( \frac{\partial f_2}{\partial y}(x,y) {@feed[4]@} \)

on_true.feedback: Well Done! The differential \( Df(x,y) \) is correct.

on_false.feedback:
The answer is partially correct!

All The partial derivatives are correct, but not on the right order in the matrix.

The right answer is \(jacobian(f, [x,y])\)
The approximation is not in the right format.

on_true.feedback:
The Approximation is correct.

The difference, by coordinates, between your estimate and the actual value of \(f({{CT:2}}+\frac{{{CT:3}}}{100},{{CT:4}}+\frac{{{CT:5}}}{100})\) is {@differ@}

on_false.feedback:
The approximation is incorrect.

We can approximate the value of the function \(f(x,y)\) around the point\(({{CT:2}},{{CT:4}})\).

\( f(x,y)=f({{CT:2}},{{CT:4}})+\begin{bmatrix} \frac{\partial f_1}{\partial x}(({{CT:2}},{{CT:4}}) & \frac{\partial f_1}{\partial y}(({{CT:2}},{{CT:4}})\\ \frac{\partial f_2}{\partial x}(({{CT:2}},{{CT:4}})& \frac{\partial f_2}{\partial y}(({{CT:2}},{{CT:4}}) \end{bmatrix} \cdot \left( \begin{bmatrix}x\\ y \end{bmatrix}- \begin{bmatrix} {{CT:2}}\\{{CT:4}} \end{bmatrix} \right) \)

Therefore,

\( f({{CT:2}}+\frac{{{CT:3}}}{100},{{CT:4}}+\frac{{{CT:5}}}{100})=f({{CT:2}},{{CT:4}})+\begin{bmatrix} \frac{\partial f_1}{\partial x}(({{CT:2}},{{CT:4}}) & \frac{\partial f_1}{\partial y}(({{CT:2}},{{CT:4}})\\ \frac{\partial f_2}{\partial x}(({{CT:2}},{{CT:4}})& \frac{\partial f_2}{\partial y}(({{CT:2}},{{CT:4}}) \end{bmatrix} \cdot \begin{bmatrix} \frac{{{CT:3}}}{100}\\\frac{{{CT:5}}}{100} \end{bmatrix}= \begin{bmatrix} {{CT:6}}\\{{CT:7}} \end{bmatrix} \)
